title: feat(spec): `ISecurityService` gains `resolveEffectiveObjectPermissions`, the effective-object-permission reader (#19539)
body:
Fixes #19539

> ⚠️ **这是一次重建。** 原 PR **#19521** 与原卡 **#19354** 随 `os-sam` 停用后不可见(PR 实测为**隐藏**而非销毁 —— 原分支上 `POST /pulls` 回 422「已存在」);分支与提交幸存。本 PR 指向**救援分支**,与原分支**同一个 sha** `afb11047`,⛔ 无重建、⛔ 无 force-push。
> 正文主体取自原 PR 创建时的原文(head `ee8f3125`),逐字保留;此后 **R2/R3** 的增量另起一节写在末尾,⛔ 未混进原文。

Fixes #19354

Clause-②: yes (widening) — one new member on a published interface. `references/contract-review.md:12` 「新导出符号或已发布载荷上的新键恒 `yes`」; the arm is `widening` because the public surface grows and no accept set narrows.

The ruled work is batch #156 item 5 letter A (`issuecomment-5725678115`, maintainer 「同意」): *"`ISecurityService` gains an effective-object-permission reader, threaded through the engine so `evaluateOptionVisibility` populates `EvalContext.permissions`; a census of every `current_user`-bound predicate evaluation site comes first"*. **That the reader is declared is settled and this PR does not re-open it.** What was genuinely open — the reader's name, parameters, return type, optionality and prose — is argued below from first-hand readings on this tree.

## What lands

One OPTIONAL member on `ISecurityService`, its contract test, and a changeset. Nothing else: 3 files, +178/-1 against merge base `48c39e002`.

The member takes only a `SecurityContext` and answers a promise of a readonly record keyed by object name whose values are `EffectiveObjectPermission` — the `objects` map of `GetEffectivePermissionsResponse`, i.e. the same bytes `/auth/me/permissions` already serves, named rather than restated so the two ends cannot drift key by key.

## The design, and the readings behind each choice

**Read first, because the engine half's requirement is not negotiable.** `@objectstack/formula` `src/types.ts:40` declares `EvalPermissions` as a readonly record of object name to `EffectiveObjectPermission`, and its docblock says it is *"the published `/auth/me/permissions` shape, verbatim"*. `src/stdlib.ts:209` is the only reader: `can()` takes `binding.permissions[object]` and hands it to `objectPermissionGrants`. So the return type is chosen to be assignable to `EvalPermissions` with **no shaping step in between** — deliberately, because a shaping step is where a permission map acquires a wrong `false`.

**Why a context-only reader and not the `(object, context)` shape every other reader here uses.** The object name is chosen by the AUTHORED PREDICATE at evaluation time, not by the caller. `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts:2150` `evaluateOptionVisibility` evaluates `opt.visibleWhen` with `{ record, previous, user }`; it has `opts.currentUser` and no idea which objects a predicate will name. A per-object reader would force the engine to guess, and a guess that comes up short does not fault: `objectPermissionGrants` (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts:208`) reads an absent entry as `false`, so the missed object answers `false` and a correct predicate silently hides an option from someone entitled to it. `EvalPermissions`' own prose reaches the same conclusion from the consumer side — *"pass the whole effective set the endpoint returned, never a hand-picked subset"*.

- **Rejected: `getEffectiveObjectPermission(object, context)`.** Rejected by the reading above — it manufactures exactly the hand-picked subset that doc forbids, and its failure mode is a silent denial rather than an error.
- **Rejected: an `objects?: string[]` narrowing parameter.** Same hazard in a smaller costume, and nothing in the engine can populate it correctly.

**Why not a caller-side fold of `resolvePermissionSetsForContext`.** That method's own docblock (`security-service.ts:372-398` on `main`) hands over its INPUT — the sets, unmerged, in resolution order — and says why: *"two consumers legitimately project different subsets of the same sets, and folding a merge in here would make this method the fourth copy of a rule"*. The merge onto one entry per object is not one of those projections. It is a single rule with a measured history of drifting (#7608, #7555, #6334, all cited in that same block), and the merge it names is live code today in `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts` (`foldWildcardSuperUser`, `seedSuperUserRestrictedObjects`, the managed-write clamp). ADR-0124 D4 puts that derivation on the server. Asking for the merged answer is therefore the non-drifting move; folding it again in the engine would be one more copy.

- **Rejected: `explain()` in a loop.** `ExplainOperation` (`packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts:49`) is an eight-member enum over ONE `(object, operation)` pair, so answering a predicate would be N objects by M verbs calls with N unknown — the same unknown-N problem, priced per call.
- **Measured, not assumed: no existing member already answers this.** #18783 listed *"whether an existing method already answers effective object bits under another name"* as NOT MEASURED. Read here member by member on `main`: `getReadFilter` answers rows, `getReadableFields`/`getMetadataReadableFields` answer columns, `resolvePermissionSetNames` answers set NAMES, `resolvePermissionSetsForContext` answers sets UNMERGED, `canExport`/`canReadObject`/`hasWriteBypass` answer one bit each, `resolveWriteScope` answers a depth, `explain` answers one pair. None answers the object-keyed effective map.

**Entries, not verdicts.** The values are the effective `allow*` plus super-user entries, not per-verb booleans, so the fold from entry to verdict stays in `objectPermissionGrants` — the one reading shared with `PermissionEvaluator.checkObjectPermission`, per that function's own docblock. Pre-folding would be a fourth copy of that rule and would destroy the distinctions the fold depends on: `allowCreate` has no super-user bypass, and `allowExport` is a conjunction (`grant` AND `read`), not a bit. The contract test asserts both cells through the real function rather than restating them.

**The wildcard is CARRIED, and absence still means "no grant".** Measured on `main`: the endpoint puts a super-user grant under the `'*'` key and folds it into named entries, and `seedSuperUserRestrictedObjects` materialises entries only for objects whose exposure is restricted — so an object no permission set mentions has no entry at all, and every reader answers "no grant" for it. The docblock states that limit instead of promising an entry per object, and says the consumer that needs the enforcement path's answer for such an object reads the `'*'` entry itself. Promising completeness here would be a claim no implementation on this tree can honour.

**Throws on resolution failure**, exactly as its two `resolve*` siblings do, and never degrades to an empty or partial map: `{}` is a REAL answer meaning "this subject holds nothing", so a failure wearing that costume is a silent denial of everything. This composes with the consumer: a throw means the engine passes nothing, and `can()` with no permission data throws loudly by design (`stdlib.ts:199`) rather than answering.

**OPTIONAL, because required would break every existing implementation.** Every member added to this interface since ADR-0106 is optional and carries an "absence is a defined state" paragraph; the file's preamble already tells consumers to feature-detect. The one thing this docblock adds is the fallback rule, because the obvious fallback is wrong: an absent method must make the consumer pass NOTHING downstream, never an empty map. An empty map is a real answer and would deny every gated option on every deployment whose security service predates this method.

## Verification

Head `ee8f3125`. Every number below was measured on this tree at that commit.

- **Gate families**: derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (82 commands once the changeset existed — 77 before it). All 82 run, each exit code captured BEFORE any pipe. Reconciled: `dispatch-gates --ran` reports **82 derived, 82 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**, a DERIVED zero because every row carries a code and none is 3.
- Four gates first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3 — the tool's own "nothing was measured" code, not a finding): `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`. The build closure they name was built (`turbo run build` over `./packages/*` and `./packages/*/*`, 72/72 tasks) and all four then exited 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` — 0. `typecheck` — 0 (source, scripts and test layers). `test` — 0, **507 files / 14859 tests passed**.
- **Consumers**: `turbo run typecheck --filter='...@objectstack/spec'` — the DEPENDENTS direction, **140/140 tasks green**.
- **Generated carriers: none moves, and that is measured rather than inspected.** `gen:api-surface`, `gen:export-origins` and `gen:declaration-map` were all re-run with the repo's own tooling and left the tree byte-identical (`git status --porcelain` empty but for the then-untracked changeset); `check:api-surface`, `check:export-origins` and `check:generated` are among the 82 green. These carriers record exported DECLARATION names, and this change adds no exported symbol — `ISecurityService` is already listed in both (`api-surface/contracts.json:151`, `export-origins/contracts.json:151`). No generated file was hand-edited.
- **Reverse verification (one-shot, no permanent artefact).** The optionality pin is not vacuous: with the fix committed, `?` was removed from the declaration through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which proved the mutation landed on disk (anchor 1 to 0, blob `b354f3fe1c70` to `325897b0dd5b`). Predicted direction: RED. Observed: `check:test-typecheck` exit 1, *"src/contracts/security-service.test.ts: 3 type error(s) in a file the ledger does not cover"*. Restored leg: blob back to `b354f3fe1c70`, `git diff HEAD` empty, same gate exit 0. No dist preflight was needed — that gate compiles `packages/spec` sources, it does not resolve through `dist/`.
- The `@ts-expect-error` directives in the test are live for the same mechanical reason: `security-service.test.ts` carries **no entry** in `packages/spec/test-typecheck-debt.json` (grep exit 1, count 0), so its error budget is zero and an unused directive would be red on its own.
- **Lint, narrowed and the narrowing proven.** Not the repo-wide `pnpm lint` scan, which is CI's run. `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the two changed TS files: **2 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings** (counts read from the JSON, not from prose). The narrowing excludes nothing because this repo's single `eslint.config.mjs` **never enables type-aware linting for any file** — no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules — stated and positively controlled in that config's own comment at `eslint.config.mjs:327`. With no cross-file type program, no verdict on an untouched file can move because of this diff. The changeset `.md` is outside every `files` glob in that config.

## Acceptance notes

- ⛔ **Declaration only — no behaviour moves.** `@objectstack/plugin-security` does not gain the method here and nothing calls it; the `packages/objectql` / `evaluateOptionVisibility` threading stays on #18783, which declares `Blocked-by:` this card. Every deployment answers exactly as it did before.
- ⛔ **The census clause of the ruling is not discharged here.** It binds the engine half: the `current_user`-bound predicate evaluation sites live in `packages/objectql`, outside this card's file surface.
- **Noted, not filed — a gap that belongs to the consumer half, not to this declaration.** `can()` reads only the named entry (`stdlib.ts:209`) and never consults `'*'`, while the effective map materialises entries only for objects some set mentions or whose exposure is restricted. A wildcard super-user therefore gets `false` from `can()` for an unmentioned, unrestricted object, where the server would allow. It is reachable only once something populates `EvalContext.permissions` server-side, which is #18783's work, and the docblock added here states the limit so whoever does that threading meets it as a documented constraint rather than as a surprise. Who picks it up: the #18783 executor.
- **Frozen instruments respected**: no gate, ratchet row or census row was added, and no test was skipped, disabled or quarantined.

## ⚠️ R2 / R3 增量 —— 原文写于 `ee8f3125`,本分支现为 `afb11047`

原文那一节的数字(`3 files, +178/-1`、`Head ee8f3125`、消融 blob)描述的是**更早的 head**,⛔ 不是本 head。本 head:**3 文件 +246/-2**,对 merge base `48c39e002`。

### R2 修的(达档复核第一次 FAIL)

- **F1** —— `.d.ts` 里两句相反指令(旧段把 `objects` 合并派给调用方并点名规则「most-permissive」,新成员却说「该问而不是自己折」)。
- **F2 / F3** —— changeset 两句假话:「列在**三个**载体里」实为两个(⭐ 告示就在句子里:说三个却只给两个锚);「the diff is **2 files**」实为 3。

### R3 修的(第二次 FAIL —— ⚠️ R2 的修补**造出了新矛盾**)

R2 新增的段落与一段**早就存在**的段落撞上了:同一个 `objects` 轴、同一个条件(服务早于该方法),**两条相反指令**,而其中一段还自称「⛔ 这两段是一条指令,不是两条」—— 按它自己的话就是假的,因为当时是**三段话、两条规则**。

⇒ R3 的解法**不是**把哪句话改模糊,而是**按消费者类别划界**:

- 自己 **SERVES** 一份投影的(`/auth/me/permissions`、`/me/apps` 端点)⇒ 保留调用方折叠;
- 只负责 **POPULATE** 一张权限图给别人回答的(引擎填 `EvalContext.permissions`)⇒ 什么都不传。

并明写选择依据:**「a consumer picks by what it does with the map rather than by which paragraph it read first」**。

**F4** 两处也修了:「更严」现在点名指称 `PermissionEvaluator.checkObjectPermission`(不点名是错的 —— 同一端点之所以还要 `clampManagedObjectWrites`,正因为该折叠在引擎写守卫面前**更松**);「另一个集合**拒绝**掉的条目」改为「非传播」,并加一句 **「most-permissive has no deny」**。

⭐ R3 还采纳了一条更强的论证:**调用方即使折叠正确也答不出来** —— 服务端的推导要读 `enable`(API 暴露)与 `managedBy`/`userActions`,那是**持有 `PermissionSet[]` 的一方根本没有**的对象 schema。

### ⚠️ 仍然欠着

- **在档复核**:本 head 上没有。
- **CI**:本 head 上 **NOT MEASURED** —— 封号发生在花名册读到之前。⛔ 不要把任何旧读数当成绿。
